# CANYO LLC

> Veteran-owned managed IT services provider serving small businesses in Tucson and Southern Arizona. CANYO builds managed IT environments designed to prevent problems before they become disruptions — automated maintenance, security monitoring, backup verification, and controlled remediation with human intervention when judgment is required. Flat-rate monthly pricing with guaranteed response times.

## Company

- [About](https://canyo.net/about/): Founder Samuel Glenn, U.S. Army veteran, prevention-first IT philosophy
- [Process](https://canyo.net/process/): Free assessment, stabilize, manage, report & review
- [Services](https://canyo.net/services/): 24/7 monitoring & maintenance, remote & on-site support, backup & recovery, security & compliance, IT documentation & asset management, new-hire onboarding, health reports & reviews
- [Pricing](https://canyo.net/pricing/): $200/user up to 10 users; $2,000 base + $150/user beyond 10; annual service agreements
- [FAQ](https://canyo.net/faq/): 23 questions covering monitoring, backups, security, pricing, compliance, remote access, and more
- [Reviews](https://canyo.net/reviews/): Early feedback, 5.0 rated on Google
- [Contact](https://canyo.net/contact/): contact@canyo.net, +1-520-336-7521
- [Inside CANYO](https://canyo.net/inside-canyo/): Technical deep-dive — least privilege, defense in depth, verification over trust, isolation by default, layered access model, incident response, reversible-first operations

## Technology Stack

- NinjaOne: Remote monitoring & management (RMM)
- Guardz: AI-native managed detection and response (MDR) with SentinelOne EDR
- Tailscale: Zero-trust remote access, SOC 2 Type II certified platform, WireGuard-based
- Restic: Encrypted, deduplicated, snapshot-based backup engine
- Backblaze B2: Immutable object storage for off-site backups
- CISO Assistant: Open-source GRC platform for compliance framework management (HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2)

## Key Differentiators

- Prevention-first: designed to prevent problems before they become disruptions
- Verification over assumption: backups verified, changes tested, outcomes documented
- Automated remediation: approved scripts handle known failures, AI-assisted analysis for tickets, human escalation for judgment calls
- Automated threat containment: SentinelOne detection triggers Tailscale network restriction
- Documented institutional memory: every device, account, configuration, and change is documented
- Compliance-ready: controls tracked against HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 using CISO Assistant
- Honest scope: no cabling, no cameras, no break/fix — managed IT only
- Transparent onboarding: published week-by-week first-30-days plan (inventory, stabilize, document, report)
- Example monthly health report published on the homepage (sample data, clearly labeled)
- Illustrative ransomware response scenario published on Inside CANYO (detect → isolate → investigate → remediate → verify)
- Published automation permission boundaries: automation handles known reversible actions; access, data, and policy changes always require human approval
